references.title: The limits of falsifiability: Dimensionality, measurement thresholds, and the sub-Landauer domain in biological systems

contexts.context: Version 2.0 clarifies the two-stage model (reversible correlation followed by irreversible projection), discusses temporal resolution as part of the measurement framework todd2025biosystems, and examines how the placement of the projection boundary constrains artificial systems.

Connection to framework formalism. The companion paper todd2025biosystems (and its v2.0 extension) defines a framework $F = (M, R, D)$ as a triple of maps: measurement $M: X Y$, representation $R: Y Z$, and decision $D: Z \0,1\$. Each framework induces a partition on the state space $X$, and projection loss $L(F) := H(X) - I(X;Z)$ quantifies how much information about $X$ is destroyed by the framework choice. Here, temporal resolution $ t$ is a component of $M$---the choice of $ t$ determines what counts as ``simultaneous'' versus ``sequential'' and thereby determines which causal relationships are visible. Framework dependence of timing (7) is a special case of the general framework dependence of falsifiability.

The companion paper on falsifiability todd2025biosystems establishes that scientific frameworks are themselves projections---axiomatic choices about what variables matter, what counts as evidence, and how questions are structured. Version 2.0 of that analysis extends this to show that falsifiability is framework-relative: a hypothesis can only be falsified with respect to a given set of background assumptions.

references.title: The thermodynamics of computation

contexts.context: Bennett (1973, 1982): Completed the resolution. The demon's memory is finite; to continue operating, it must erase old measurements. This erasure cost exactly compensates the work extracted. The second law is saved bennett1982.

Energy dissipated during tracking: $E_digital (160--332) T 2 4.610^-19$--$9.5 10^-19$ J (ideal Landauer floor; practical CMOS is typically far higher, while fully reversible logic can approach the floor only with severe speed and noise-tolerance tradeoffs bennett1982,horowitz2014)

Efficiency gain: $ 160$--$330$ at the theoretical Landauer limit. In practice the gap is much larger because contemporary digital hardware operates well above that floor horowitz2014. Reversible computing can, in principle, narrow the gap bennett1982, but only with substantial speed and noise-tolerance tradeoffs. Digital architectures pay per recorded bit; continuous substrates defer recording and pay at projection. Analog and neuromorphic systems gain efficiency to the extent that they also defer discretization.

Bennett bennett1982 established that logical reversibility bounds energy only if computation is quasi-static and low-noise. Still et al. still2012 showed predictive information confers thermodynamic advantage, but creating/storing it has minimal work cost. Kolchinsky & Wolpert kolchinsky2018 demonstrated that minimal work depends on changes in non-equilibrium distributions—aligning with our Projection Bound via $ N_$ and KL terms.

To know what water does, use water. To know what a protein does, use a protein. To know what neurons do, use neurons. Digital simulation incurs exponential state-space costs for many such tasks, though reversible computing may asymptotically approach thermodynamic bounds with severe speed and noise-tolerance tradeoffs bennett1982,frank2019.
